# Classification and special values

Telling NaNs, infinities, zeros, subnormals and normal values apart, and making the special ones.

<h2 id="float-class"><code>FloatClass</code></h2>

```rux
pub enum FloatClass: int32 {
    NotANumber = 0,
    Infinite = 1,
    Zero = 2,
    Subnormal = 3,
    Normal = 4
}
```

The five kinds IEEE 754 sorts every value into.
`Copy`.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Math/Src/Classify.rux#L28)

**Cases**

| Name         | Value | Description                                                                          |
| ------------ | ----- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `NotANumber` | `0`   | Not a number: the result of an operation with no meaningful answer.                  |
| `Infinite`   | `1`   | One of the two infinities.                                                           |
| `Zero`       | `2`   | Positive or negative zero.                                                           |
| `Subnormal`  | `3`   | A value too small to carry a full significand, whose precision degrades toward zero. |
| `Normal`     | `4`   | An ordinary value at full precision.                                                 |

<h2 id="is-nan"><code>IsNan</code></h2>

```rux
pub func IsNan(value: float64) -> bool
pub func IsNan(value: float32) -> bool
```

Whether `value` is a NaN.
A NaN is the only value not equal to itself, which is why this needs no bit pattern.

| Overload                                 | Summary                                                     |
| ---------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `pub func IsNan(value: float64) -> bool` | Whether `value` is a NaN.                                   |
| `pub func IsNan(value: float32) -> bool` | Determines whether `value` is a NaN at `float32` precision. |

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Math/Src/Classify.rux#L46)

**Parameters**

| Name    | Type                  | Description   |
| ------- | --------------------- | ------------- |
| `value` | `float64` / `float32` | value to test |

**Returns**: `true` when `value` is a NaN

<h2 id="is-zero"><code>IsZero</code></h2>

```rux

pub func IsZero(value: float32) -> bool
```

Whether `value` is either zero.
Both zeros answer `true`; [`SignBit`](/docs/api/math/classification#sign-bit) is what tells them apart.

| `pub func IsZero(value: float32) -> bool` | Determines whether `value` is either signed zero at `float32` precision. |

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Math/Src/Classify.rux#L95)

**Parameters**

| Name    | Type                  | Description   |
| ------- | --------------------- | ------------- |
| `value` | `float64` / `float32` | value to test |

**Returns**: `true` when `value` is positive or negative zero

<h2 id="is-normal"><code>IsNormal</code></h2>

```rux
pub func IsNormal(value: float64) -> bool
pub func IsNormal(value: float32) -> bool
```

Whether `value` is an ordinary value at full precision.
Zero is **not** normal, which surprises people and is the definition every IEEE 754 implementation uses.

| Overload                                    | Summary                                                      |
| ------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `pub func IsNormal(value: float64) -> bool` | Whether `value` is an ordinary value at full precision.      |
| `pub func IsNormal(value: float32) -> bool` | Determines whether `value` is normal at `float32` precision. |

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Math/Src/Classify.rux#L130)

**Parameters**

| Name    | Type                  | Description   |
| ------- | --------------------- | ------------- |
| `value` | `float64` / `float32` | value to test |

**Returns**: `true` when `value` is normal

<h2 id="sign-bit"><code>SignBit</code></h2>

```rux
pub func SignBit(value: float64) -> bool
pub func SignBit(value: float32) -> bool
```

Whether `value`'s sign bit is set.
This is the sign bit, not a comparison: `SignBit(-0.0)` is `true` where `-0.0 < 0.0` is false, and a negative NaN
answers `true` where every comparison against it answers false. That is the whole reason to ask by bit.

| Overload                                   | Summary                                                                   |
| ------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `pub func SignBit(value: float64) -> bool` | Whether `value`'s sign bit is set.                                        |
| `pub func SignBit(value: float32) -> bool` | Determines whether the sign bit of `value` is set at `float32` precision. |

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Math/Src/Classify.rux#L174)

**Parameters**

| Name    | Type                  | Description                   |
| ------- | --------------------- | ----------------------------- |
| `value` | `float64` / `float32` | value whose sign is inspected |

**Returns**: `true` when the sign bit is set
